Specialized variants are needed to render important structures differently if they lie within a clipped area [S7].

The claim states that specialized variants (splitting the pipeline into two stages) are needed to render important structures differently if they lie within a clipped area. The evidence explicitly states that without this solution, structures excluded from clipping cannot be shown in a different visualization style because rendering parameters can only be changed globally. It then describes the solution: splitting the pipeline into two parallel stages, where the second stage specifies specific rendering parameters for important structures that lie in the clipping area. This directly supports the claim.

The evidence explicitly states in Source [S6] that 'each voxel within the volume is classified by one or more transfer functions and an opacity and a color is assigned to each of them.' It further explains that 'unwanted data values are faded out and get an opacity of zero.' This confirms that the transfer functions define the mapping from the data values (scalar values) to color and opacity.

January 1988 falls within the 'late 1980s'. *   **Limitations:** Blurring in pre-classification methods; high cost of per-voxel shading and interpolation; global clipping limitations in standard pipelines [S2, unofficial][S6][S7].

The claim contains three specific points. 1. 'Blurring in pre-classification methods': Source [S2] describes a method where shading and classification are separate steps, and [S6] describes a pipeline where classification happens first (pre-classification) using transfer functions. While [S6] mentions 'trilinear interpolation' which causes blurring, it does not explicitly label this as a 'limitation of pre-classification methods' in the provided text, nor does [S2] discuss 'pre-classification' limitations specifically regarding blurring (it focuses on independence of shading/classification). However, the general concept of interpolation blurring is present. 2. 'High cost of per-voxel shading and interpolation': Source [S6] explicitly states: 'Because of the high cost of performance of shading and interpolation between the eight voxels of a cell, these functions can be switched off.' This supports this part of the claim. 3. 'Global clipping limitations in standard pipelines': Source [S7] explicitly discusses this limitation: 'we are not able to show these structures in a different visualization style because the rendering parameters can just be changed globally'. This supports the third part. Since the first part ('Blurring in pre-classification methods') is not explicitly supported as a limitation in the provided text (though implied by interpolation), while the other two are explicitly supported, the verdict is partial.
